title: Recipe 20 — Secrets Management (three backends, one rotation contract)

beats.label: Open the recipe
beats.cue: “Recipe 20 is for rotation without restart — daemons holding long-lived channel credentials, gateway JWT secrets, audit encryption keys. If you only have $VAR_NAME straight to env, you are already using the env-var backend without naming it.”

beats.label: Start from a blank spec
beats.cue: live/ is scratch — the committed recipe and starters are never touched by a take.

beats.label: Clear the file backend
beats.cue: “The file backend stores under .crewhaus/secrets — scratch here, so a re-take starts from nothing stored.”

verify.note: idempotent — makes the take repeatable so the doctor counts below are the ones on camera

beats.label: Load the API key
beats.cue: [needs-key] Sources demos/.env. Note what it does not contain: the Slack credentials this spec declares.

groups.title: Beat 1 · a spec whose every secret is a $VAR_NAME

beats.label: Type the channel starter
beats.cue: “The recipe's own wiring example, committed: botToken and signingSecret as $VAR_NAME references. Never a literal in the spec — that is rule one.”

beats.label: Lint it
beats.cue: “Clean. A $VAR_NAME is spec surface the compiler understands, not a string it happens to leave alone.”

beats.label: Show the lowered IR
beats.cue: “The references survive lowering as references. The compiler has not resolved them and never will — resolution is a runtime read.”

verify.note: prints the IR for target channel — the $VAR_NAME refs intact

beats.label: Compile the daemon — and check it
beats.cue: “GREEN, and read the gate name: boot reached its spec env refs gate. --check knows the only thing missing is a credential this spec itself declares.”

verify.note: GREEN — assertion ok (4 anchors); install ok; boot gated (boot reached its spec env refs gate)

beats.label: Find the startup-time null check
beats.cue: “There is the lowering the recipe prints: process.env read, or throwMissing at startup. A missing secret crashes the daemon before it binds — not at first inbound request with an undefined.”

beats.label: Check every secret the daemon boots on
beats.cue: “Run this before deploying. Every env var the daemon needs, checked with no network — and it exits non-zero on purpose, because a missing secret at deploy time is cheaper than at first traffic.”
beats.command: env -u SLACK_BOT_TOKEN -u SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET crewhaus channel verify live/crewhaus.yaml --offline

verify.note: deliberate rejection, exit 1 — the two Slack refs are scrubbed explicitly because the Setup group already sourced .env into this same shell. Names each failure and what it costs: “the daemon exits at boot without it”

beats.label: Now supply all three
beats.cue: “Same gate, every reference satisfied: exit zero. --offline checks presence, not validity — no platform probe ran, so these values do not have to be real to prove the wiring.”
beats.command: env SLACK_BOT_TOKEN=xoxb-demo-not-real SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET=demo-signing-secret-not-real ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN=sk-ant-demo-not-real crewhaus channel verify live/crewhaus.yaml --offline

verify.note: 3 check(s), 0 failed — set inline via env so the fake values never leak into the beats after this one

groups.title: Beat 4 · the file backend and a real rotation

beats.label: Ask the file backend what it knows
beats.cue: “Backend: file, and nothing stored yet. Note what doctor prints — names, backend, status. It never prints values.”

beats.label: Rotate the signing secret
beats.cue: “Atomic write via tempfile and rename, then every subscriber's onRotation handler fires with the name — never the value. They call get() themselves.”
beats.command: crewhaus secrets rotate SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET --value s3cr3t-rotated-0001 --backend file

verify.note: rotated SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET (19 chars) via file backend

beats.label: Check the file mode
beats.cue: “Owner-only, 0600. And the name went through a path-traversal guard — a slash, a dot-dot or a null byte is rejected, not sanitized.”

beats.label: Ask the backend again
beats.cue: “One secret known, by name only. That listing is the compliance artefact: who accessed what, when — without ever handing the auditor the secret.”

verify.note: backend: file · known: 1 secret(s) — SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET, metadata only

beats.label: Boot the channel daemon
beats.cue: [needs-key] “Needs the real Slack pair plus a Claude credential. The Slack adapter subscribes to its signing-secret rotation as it comes up.”

verify.note: needs SLACK_BOT_TOKEN + SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET and Anthropic credentials

beats.label: Rotate under the running daemon
beats.cue: [needs-key] “No restart, no redeploy. The HMAC verifier picks up the new key on the next request; requests already in flight finish against the old one.”
beats.command: CREWHAUS_SECRETS_BACKEND=file crewhaus secrets rotate SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET --value s3cr3t-rotated-0002 --backend file

verify.note: the rotation itself is keyless — what needs a key is the running daemon this beat is proving picks it up

beats.label: Stop the daemon
beats.cue: [needs-key] Job %1 is the daemon the boot beat backgrounded — skip this and the take leaves a process holding the channel port.

verify.note: kills the backgrounded daemon from the run-boot beat

groups.title: One more thing · the rotation, audited

beats.label: Run the recipe's Try-it smoke
beats.cue: “Probe 5 is recipe 20's own end-to-end: rotate through the file backend, then assert a secrets_rotation record landed in the tenant's audit log and every onRotation listener fired.”

verify.note: all probes passed — probe 5 asserts the secrets_rotation audit record under the configured tenant. Redirected rather than piped so the exit code is the smoke's own

beats.label: Read the probe log
beats.cue: “Hash-chained into the tenant's audit JSONL, which is what lets the trail prove who accessed which secret when. Vault swaps in by one env var — the spec does not change.”
